description: The same weekly open electronics night at the Mission hackerspace in the quiet week between Christmas and New Year: soldering stations, test gear and people tinkering on robotics and embedded projects. Beginners are welcome to come and learn.

title: Man or Astro-man? with The Subsonics
description: Cult sci-fi surf-rock instrumentalists Man or Astro-man? play their famously theatrical live show, with Atlanta garage band The Subsonics. All ages, doors 8pm.

title: Bachata Tuesday Class & Social (last Tuesday)
description: A monthly bachata night: a 7pm class (intermediate-leaning) with Bryon & Samm, then social dancing to DJ Thiencito until 11. No partner required.

title: Tuesday Skate Theme Night at the Church of 8 Wheels
description: A themed adult roller-disco night in a converted church, run by SF's 'Godfather of Skate', D. Miles Jr. It's a good dead-week outing between Christmas and New Year.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The year's last Woodchopper's Ball at the Verdi Club: live swing band, a drop-in beginner lesson 9-9:15pm, and no partner needed.

title: Man or Astro-man? with The Subsonics
description: Space-age surf-rock cult heroes from Alabama play the small Potrero Hill room, with Atlanta garage-punk trio The Subsonics and DJ Sid Presley on surf and 60s records. Doors 8pm, music 9pm, all ages.

title: Figure drawing at Monument SF (Sketchboard Co.)
description: Sketchboard Co.'s Wednesday drop-in life drawing session with a live model at Monument in SoMa, running two hours with short and long poses. All levels are welcome.

title: Alamo Drafthouse: When Harry Met Sally...
description: Alamo's ring-in-the-new-year screening of the Nora Ephron/Rob Reiner rom-com, which builds to its famous New Year's Eve party. It's a low-key night out between the holidays.

title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night at The Function
venue: The Function SF: Comedy Club & Cocktail Lounge
price: Free with Eventbrite RSVP ($20 door; 2-drink minimum)
description: The nightly HellaFunny stand-up showcase at The Function, a cheap night out in the quiet week between Christmas and New Year. 4-5 comics, 70-90 minutes, 21+, with a two-drink minimum.

title: SF Chamber Orchestra: Rising Stars, A New Year's Celebration (free)
address: 401 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: The SF Chamber Orchestra's free New Year concert featuring young soloists, closing with Mozart's 'Jupiter' Symphony, in the War Memorial's Herbst Theatre.

title: Berkeley Wednesday Contra Dance (5th Wednesday)
price: $20 ($15 members, $6 students; pay what you can)
description: BACDS contra with caller Andy Shore and live music from Christopher Jacoby and Corey Walters. The intro lesson is at 7:30pm and roles are gender-neutral. BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley takes ~25 min, plus a 10-min walk.

title: Japanese New Year Bell-Ringing Ceremony (41st annual)
description: Visitors take turns striking the museum's 2,100-pound 16th-century Japanese temple bell 108 times, with a chant and short Dharma talk. Numbered tickets to ring the bell are handed out from noon at Samsung Hall.

title: BACDS New Year's Eve Contra Ball
venue: First United Methodist Church of Palo Alto
description: A four-hour New Year's Eve contra ball with caller Susan Petrick and fiddle and guitar from Will Wheeler and Ben Jackson. It's the most ceilidh-like way to see in the new year. Palo Alto is about an hour by Caltrain from 4th & King, so check the late trains home.

title: BATS Improv: Noir New Year's
venue: BATS Bayfront Theatre, Fort Mason Center
address: 2 Marina Blvd, Building B, 3rd Floor, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: A one-night-only, fully improvised film-noir comedy caper with champagne for New Year's Eve. It's done by 10pm, so there's time to head to the Embarcadero fireworks after.

title: The Lemon Twigs New Year's Eve, with Tchotchke
description: The D'Addario brothers' '60s/'70s-style power-pop band ring in 2027 in the Chapel's converted mortuary hall, with Tchotchke and a DJ. All ages, standing.

title: A Very Purple New Year's Eve: Purple Rain (4K) + Sign O' the Times at the Vogue
description: The Vogue's third annual Prince-themed NYE: doors at 9pm with Prince videos, a 4K restoration of Purple Rain at 10pm, a midnight countdown with complimentary champagne, then the Sign O' the Times concert film. A New Year's Eve that isn't a club night.

title: New Year's Eve fireworks on the Embarcadero
description: The city's free midnight fireworks over the Bay. Arrive by about 11:30pm and stand along the Embarcadero south of the Ferry Building; Muni is usually free late on NYE.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Making Waves on the Waterfront (New Year's Day)
address: Foot of Market St at The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: A flat 1.5-2 hour New Year's Day walk along the northern waterfront covering Gold Rush pioneers, inventors and labor organizers, ending at Levi Plaza. It meets in front of the Ferry Building under the clock tower.

title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night: New Year's Day show
venue: The Function SF: Comedy Club & Cocktail Lounge
price: Free with Eventbrite RSVP ($25 door; 2-drink minimum)
description: A low-key New Year's Day night out: the HellaFunny nightly stand-up showcase at The Function on Market St. There's also a 9pm show; 21+.

title: About Last Night: one-night-stand storytelling show
description: Real people tell true stories about horrifying one-night stands, awkward hookups and regrettable romps, which suits New Year's Day. Doors 7pm, show 8pm.

title: Bachata Lab: Friday bachata classes (3 levels) + social (New Year's Day)
description: The weekly Friday bachata night runs on New Year's Day: concurrent beginner, intermediate and advanced classes from 8pm with partner rotation, then social dancing until 1am.

title: The Board Walks: Walk & Talk About Life's Big Questions
description: A weekly 5-mile walking conversation club for people who want depth over small talk. Everyone brings a question to explore, shares it in an opening circle, then drifts between small conversations on the walk. It's newcomer-friendly and runs rain or shine.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Castro, Tales of the Village
address: Castro St & Market St, San Francisco, CA 94114
description: A free volunteer-led two-hour history walk through the Castro, from Harvey Milk's camera-shop campaign to how the neighbourhood keeps evolving. It starts at Jane Warner Plaza.

title: The Commons monthly picnic in Alamo Square
address: Alamo Square Park, San Francisco, CA
description: The SF Commons' monthly picnic with blankets, shared snacks, lawn games and a surprise live band in the second half. It's an easy, drop-in way to meet the Hayes Valley community crowd, and +1s are welcome.

title: Saturday adult roller disco at the Church of 8 Wheels
description: The adults-only Saturday night session of SF's roller disco in a former church, four hours of funk and disco on wheels. It's an easy first Saturday of the year.

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with a free beginner lesson from Hep Jen at noon. Partners rotate, so you don't need to bring one. Weather permitting.

title: Lightscape at SF Botanical Garden (final night)
venue: San Francisco Botanical Garden (Golden Gate Park)
description: A one-mile after-dark trail of a million lights, light sculptures and sound through the Botanical Garden, on its last night of the season. Timed entry runs from 5pm to 8:30pm, so book ahead.

title: Monthly Reflection Jam at The Commons
description: A first-Sunday evening of guided journaling prompts about the past month. You can choose to share your reflections in a small group ('Mingling Muser') or journal on your own. It's a gentle, conversation-based way to start the year with new people.

title: SF Salsa Social: beginner class + salsa & mambo dancing
description: New Year's first-Sunday salsa social at the Verdi Club: a beginner class at 7pm, then salsa and mambo dancing until 11:30. A good fresh-start night out.

title: Figure drawing Mondays at Sin Miedo Gallery (Sketchboard)
description: Sketchboard Co.'s two-hour drop-in life drawing session with a live model in a Mission gallery. All levels are welcome; bring your own paper and pencils.

title: SalsaCrazy Mondays: salsa lesson + salsa/bachata dancing
description: The first SalsaCrazy Monday of 2027 (and the start of the January progressive series). A beginner salsa lesson with no partner needed, then salsa and bachata dancing at a real club. 21+.

title: Contact Improvisation class + jam at The Castro Room
description: SF's 1st and 3rd Monday contact improv night: an hour's beginner-friendly class from 7:45pm flows into a jam with live music until 10:15pm. Teachers and hosts rotate; the SF CI WhatsApp group posts who's on. First Monday after New Year — confirm it's running in the SF CI WhatsApp group before going.

title: ALTERNA: new wave and goth skate night at the Church of 8 Wheels
description: A Tuesday roller-skating night in the converted church, with new wave, darkwave, synthpop and post-punk under the disco ball. Rent skates at the door if you don't have your own.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). New monthly Lindy Hop and Balboa class series usually start the first Tuesday of the month (7-9pm, before the dance). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: Matchbook-Neon Typography Tour (SF Neon + Letterform Archive)
venue: Meet on first block of Ellis St (across from Tad's Steaks)
description: A 90-minute evening walk from Market St to Union Square hunting vintage neon signs, led by SF Neon with Letterform Archive's Stephen Coles. It covers mid-century nightlife history through old signs and matchbook typography.

title: Hayes Valley Comedy Night at The Function
price: Free with Eventbrite RSVP ($20-$30 at door; 2-drink minimum)
description: A midweek stand-up showcase with 4-5 local comics at The Function on Market St.

title: Berkeley Wednesday Contra Dance
price: $20 ($15 members, $6 students; pay what you can)
description: BACDS contra with caller Doe Taryn and live music from Leah Wollenberg and Jeremy Reinhard. The intro lesson is at 7:30pm and roles are gender-neutral. BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley takes ~25 min, plus a 10-min walk.

title: Sab Star with Gloomhead and swell foop
description: An all-Bay Area indie bill: San Jose shoegaze/dream-pop project Sab Star, SF post-rock five-piece Gloomhead and Berkeley indie-rock trio swell foop. Doors 7:30pm, show 8pm, all ages.

title: SF First Thursday Art Walk (Tenderloin + Lower Nob Hill)
venue: Galleries across the Tenderloin + Lower Nob Hill
description: A monthly self-guided evening of open galleries, artist-run spaces and local businesses across the Tenderloin and Lower Nob Hill. It's free and easy to drop in and out of.

title: Somatic Breathwork at The Commons
description: A guided somatic breathwork session at The Commons community space in Hayes Valley. See the Luma page for details.

title: The Loved Ones: Latest Hits record release, with The Vesuvians
description: The '90s Bay Area mod/R&B band (singer Bart Davenport, Cake's Xan McCurdy) celebrates a new record, with The Vesuvians featuring Karina Deniké and DJ Russell Quan. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: Milonga Malevaje (Thursday tango at the Verdi Club)
description: The Verdi Club's weekly Thursday Argentine tango milonga, a social dance night in the Mission's old Italian clubhouse. It's a good first Thursday back after the holidays.

title: La Hora Feliz: Friday Spanish conversation meetup
description: A relaxed weekly all-Spanish conversation hour for learners and native speakers at a Valencia St cafe. There's no cover. Newcomers are told to arrive around 6:30pm and ask at the counter for the group.

title: Cooking class: Make Your Own Sushi (CocuSocial)
description: A hands-on two-hour class with Chef Huong: you make sushi rice, then cut and roll your own maki. It's for groups of 12-26, and drinks are sold at the hotel bar (not BYOB).

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey in 70mm
description: Kubrick's masterpiece on a 70mm print in the restored 1922 Castro Theatre, a start-of-year big-screen event. All ages; doors 7pm. The ticket price is behind TicketWeb's bot wall.

title: Western Standard Time Ska Orchestra featuring Karina Deniké
description: A big-band ska, rocksteady and early-reggae orchestra with singer Karina Deniké, made for dancing in the Chapel's converted mortuary hall. Doors 8pm, show 9pm.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Welcome to San Francisco (for newcomers)
venue: Harry Bridges Plaza (across from the Ferry Building)
address: The Embarcadero at Market St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: A volunteer-led two-hour introductory walk designed for people new to the city. It goes from the Ferry Building to North Beach, covering the Gold Rush, cable cars, the 1906 quake, counterculture and food culture, and ends near North Beach cafes.

title: Chinatown SF Neon Walking Tour
venue: Chinatown YMCA (meeting point, on the sidewalk)
description: A twilight walk through Chinatown's back alleys with the San Francisco Neon authors Al Barna and Randall Ann Homan, looking at ghost signs and vintage neon. It ends at dusk with the restored Golden Star Radio sign on Clay Street.

title: Anna von Hausswolff with KatzPascale
description: SOLD OUT (per The List, 9 Nov). The Swedish singer and organist plays towering, cathedral-sized drone-pop. Mostly standing; doors 7pm.

title: Swirlies with Seko
description: The Boston shoegaze and indie-rock cult band at the Chapel (folkYEAH! presents). Doors 7pm.

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with Hep Jen's free beginner lesson at noon. No partner or experience is needed. It's weather permitting, so check the site that morning in January.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Embarcadero South, A Turbulent Port
venue: Mission & Steuart Streets, by Rincon Center (meeting point)
address: Mission St & Steuart St, San Francisco, CA 94105
description: A free two-hour waterfront history walk starting a few blocks from home. It covers the 150-year-old seawall, the Hills Bros. Coffee building, Rincon Annex and the 1934 longshore strike memorials, on the stretch where the Embarcadero Freeway once stood.

title: Purpose Alignment Circle at The Commons
description: A free small-group Purpose Alignment Circle at The Commons community space in Hayes Valley. See the Luma page for the format.

title: Crafting in the Castro: notebook making
venue: Eureka Valley/Harvey Milk Memorial Branch Library
address: 1 Jose Sarria Ct, San Francisco, CA 94114
description: A free hour-long library craft session where you bind your own notebook and take it home. Drop-in, limited to the first 15 people to arrive.

title: Irish partner dancing with live music (free beginner lesson) at O'Reilly's
description: A monthly second-Sunday Irish set-dancing night, the closest thing in SF to a ceilidh. A beginner lesson at 5pm walks you through the steps, then live-music dancing starts at 6pm. 21+.

title: Nora Brown with Stephanie Coleman
description: Young Brooklyn banjo player Nora Brown, one of the most acclaimed voices in Appalachian old-time music, with fiddler Stephanie Coleman. An intimate folkYEAH! show; all ages, doors 7pm.

title: SalsaCrazy Mondays: salsa lesson + salsa/bachata social
description: A long-running Monday salsa night: a beginner lesson at 7pm (no partner or experience needed), intermediate at 7:45, then salsa and bachata social dancing from 8:30. 21+.

title: National Theatre Live: The Audience (Helen Mirren)
description: Helen Mirren as Elizabeth II in Peter Morgan's Olivier- and Tony-winning play about the Queen's private weekly meetings with her prime ministers. It's back in cinemas for the first time in over a decade.

title: An Evening with Robyn Hitchcock: Stranded in the Future (City Lights)
description: The English psychedelic-folk songwriter Robyn Hitchcock talks about his book 'Stranded in the Future' at City Lights. A free in-store event.

title: Free bluegrass jam & concert at Blondie's
description: Blondie's weekly Monday night of local bluegrass on Valencia St, a short concert followed by an open jam. Free with an Eventbrite RSVP.

title: Happy Endings: writers' showdown at the Make-Out Room
description: Five writers perform new work on a shared theme, competing for the approval of an appointed committee. A literary night with a comedy edge in a Mission bar.

title: Cartoonist Conspiracy SF: collaborative comic drawing jam
description: A monthly meet-up where about 15 cartoonists, pros and beginners alike, pass pages around to draw a 12-page jam comic together. It's an easy, sociable way into SF's drawing scene, no skills required.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: Figure drawing at Monument SF (Sketchboard Co.)
description: A two-hour drop-in life drawing session with a model, run by Sketchboard Co. in SoMa. All levels are welcome; bring your own materials and book ahead on Square.

title: Write Night at The Commons (January)
description: A weekly writers' meetup: introductions at 6:55, an hour of quiet writing from 7pm, then a progress check-in and time to socialise. All kinds of writing are welcome.

title: An Evening with Peter Rowan: Walls of Time (City Lights)
description: Bluegrass veteran Peter Rowan, who played with Bill Monroe and in Old & In the Way, talks about his memoir 'Walls of Time: Tales of a Bluegrass Pilgrim'. It's a free in-store event; seats are first come, first served.

title: Mid-Week Merriment skate: Rivals on Ice at Union Square
venue: Safeway Holiday Ice Rink, Union Square
description: A themed 8:30pm skate inspired by hockey rivalries: wear your team colours for high-energy music and photo moments. It's one of the last themed nights before the rink closes on 18 Jan.

title: Second Thursdays figure drawing at El Rio (Sketchboard Co.)
description: Sketchboard's monthly life drawing night at the Mission's El Rio bar costs $15. It's more social than a studio session, so you can draw with a drink in hand.

title: Immersion (Colin Newman of Wire + Malka Spigel) at Gray Area
description: Electronic duo Immersion, made up of Wire's Colin Newman and Minimal Compact's Malka Spigel, play the Mission's restored Grand Theater art-and-tech space.

title: LSD and the Search for God with Cryogeyser
description: The cult shoegaze band plays a rare headline set, with dream-pop band Cryogeyser in support. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: Cooking class: Authentic Asian Dumplings (CocuSocial)
description: A hands-on two-hour class making dumpling wrappers from scratch plus pork-chive-shrimp and tofu fillings. You cook in small groups of 2-4, so it's easy to come alone (21+).

title: Bachata Lab: Friday bachata classes (3 levels) + social
description: Weekly Friday bachata (sensual/fusion) with concurrent beginner, intermediate and advanced classes from 8pm, partners rotating every minute. Social dancing runs 9:30pm-1am.

title: Seb Lowe with Kate Couriel
description: English singer-songwriter Seb Lowe brings his 2027 US tour to the small Hayes Valley room, with Kate Couriel supporting (presented by Popscene). All ages, doors 8pm.

title: The 16th Annual Bowie Bash
description: The 16th annual Bowie birthday-month bash: a costumed Bowie tribute band (billed on The List as the First Church of the Sacred Silversexual) plus drag, burlesque and puppetry, in a room built for dancing. Night one of two (Sat Jan 16 too); doors 8pm.

title: Tea Class & Tasting at Tap Twice Tea
description: A hands-on Saturday-morning workshop on tea history, varieties and brewing, with a guided tasting of one tea from each of five categories. It's taught by Jody, who has sourced tea in Asia since 2009.

title: Predicting Our Futures: Black feminist zine-making workshop
address: 401 Van Ness Ave, Suite 126, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: The Black Feminist Book Club leads a hands-on workshop making a 'future-forecasting' zine using Octavia Butler's rules for predicting the future. It runs alongside the Arts Commission gallery's show 'Excavating Uranus, A Psalm for Nyota Uhura'.

title: YBCA World of Black Film: Burning an Illusion (free, SF Art Week)
description: A free screening of Menelik Shabazz's 1981 London-set drama about a young Black woman's political awakening. It's part of Ashley Clark's curated series, with snacks and gallery entry included.

title: Social & Economic Justice Music and the Arts Festival: evening concert
description: A one-day festival at the historic Victoria Theatre bringing musicians, poets and community organisers together. Workshops run 9am-7pm, then an all-genres concert at 7pm.

title: The 16th Annual Bowie Bash (night 2: Band Picks)
description: Night two of GAMH's annual Bowie birthday-month bash, where Bowie tribute band the First Church of the Sacred Silversexual plays the band's own favourite Bowie songs. Doors 8pm, show 9:30pm.

title: Contact Improvisation class with Dai & Wei at ODC
description: A weekly Sunday-afternoon contact improvisation class at ODC in the Mission, taught by Daiane Lopes da Silva and Weidong Yang. A good way into SF's CI scene.

title: Laser cutter safety training at Noisebridge
description: A two-hour hands-on class on the hackerspace's 150W CO2 laser cutter, covering hazards, safe operation and fire response. Everyone cuts a cardboard piece, and it's the prerequisite for using the cutter on your own projects. Seats are limited.

title: Artist & curator talk: Rael San Fratello at YBCA
description: Ronald Rael and Virginia San Fratello, the design duo known for 3D-printed earth architecture and the Teeter-Totter Wall, talk about their YBCA exhibition 'Prototypes and Provocations'. Curator René Morales then moderates a conversation with them.

title: Improv(e) Your Dating Life: improv-based dating workshop
description: A two-hour Sunday workshop led by improv and dating coach Dylan Garcia that mixes improv games with dating tips to build confidence and presence. It's open to all adults 18+, and you meet other singles along the way.

title: Mucha Salsa+ social (free beginner class)
description: A not-for-profit Sunday salsa social at the Verdi Club. Beginner and intermediate salsa classes run 7-8pm and are included, then there's DJ social dancing until 11:30pm, so it's easy to come solo.

title: Thomas Lennon & Friends Sing The Smiths (SF Sketchfest)
description: Thomas Lennon and the Sweet and Tender Hooligans play Smiths songs ('Strangeways, Here We Come' at 40) with guests including David Cross, Bob Odenkirk and Chris Gethard. Doors at 7pm, show at 8pm.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Russian Hill Stairways (MLK Day)
venue: Mason & Vallejo, bottom of the Vallejo Street Steps (meeting point)
address: Mason St at Vallejo St, San Francisco, CA 94133
description: A knee-testing stairway walk over Russian Hill on the MLK Day holiday, with big views and stories of Willis Polk and Ina Coolbrith. It usually ends at Francisco Park; wear sturdy shoes.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Beat Generation in SF (MLK Day)
address: 600 Montgomery St (NW corner of plaza, by the flagpoles), San Francisco, CA 94111
description: A 1.5-hour holiday-Monday walk through the North Beach haunts of Ginsberg, Kerouac and Ferlinghetti, ending at Caffe Trieste. It passes City Lights on the way.

title: Tara Clerkin Trio
description: The Bristol trio's hazy, hypnotic mix of avant-folk, dub-tinged jazz and chamber pop, co-presented by KALW in a 350-cap room on an MLK Day evening. Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: Drop-In Circling Workshop (Berkeley)
description: January's in-person drop-in circling and authentic relating evening from The Circling Institute, open to newcomers. Register ahead: doors 6:45pm and close at 7:10pm sharp. East Bay: BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley (~25 min), then bus or bike to West Berkeley.

title: Critical Hit: board-game comedy showcase (SF Sketchfest)
description: Oakland's long-running stand-up showcase from a board-game shop brings local comics and a prize raffle to a small Valencia St room for Sketchfest. Tickets go on sale 15 Nov at 10am.

title: True Widow
description: The Dallas trio's slow, heavy 'stonegaze' (shoegaze meets stoner rock, with boy/girl vocals) in the ornate Tenderloin music hall. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: Figure drawing at Monument SF (Sketchboard Co.)
description: Sketchboard Co.'s Wednesday drop-in life drawing session with a live model at Monument in SoMa, running two hours with short and long poses. All levels are welcome.

title: In a Nutshell Storytelling (SF Sketchfest)
description: Sacramento's artist-run true-story night brings its open, community feel to the Punch Line during Sketchfest. Real people tell personal stories, and the hosts pitch it as being for anyone craving connection.

title: Berkeley Wednesday Contra Dance (The Flagstones)
price: $20 ($15 members, $6 students; pay what you can)
description: BACDS contra with caller Charlie Fenton and live band The Flagstones (Anne Goess, Charlie Hancock, Will Wheeler). The intro lesson is at 7:30pm and roles are gender-neutral. BART from Montgomery to Downtown Berkeley takes ~25 min, plus a 10-min walk.

title: Dona Murad: Librae (Omnivore Books author talk)
address: 3885A Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
description: The founder of New York's cult bakery Librae talks about her debut cookbook of Bahraini-meets-Danish pastries, from za'atar sourdough to loomi babka. It's a free in-store event with first-come seating.

title: Vijay Iyer & Wadada Leo Smith: an evening of duets
description: Pianist Vijay Iyer (a MacArthur fellow) and avant-garde trumpeter Wadada Leo Smith play duets from their two ECM albums, including 2025's Defiant Life.

title: Milonga Malevaje (Thursday tango at the Verdi Club)
description: The weekly Argentine tango milonga on the Verdi Club's historic sprung dance floor. It's a social dance for those who already know some tango, and also a good place to watch and meet the local scene.

title: Trestles (Santa Cruz surf-psych) at Cafe du Nord
description: Santa Cruz surf/psych/garage band steeped in 1960s West Coast sounds, in the basement room under the Swedish American Hall. Doors 7pm, show 8pm, all ages.

title: Eliane Elias Quartet: Antônio Carlos Jobim Centennial Celebration
description: The Brazilian pianist-singer marks 100 years of Tom Jobim with a bossa nova programme in SFJAZZ's main hall. Runs Jan 22-24, and the Sunday is 'The Art of Bossa Nova'.

title: Fruition: Something More, The Final Tour, with Rainbow Girls
description: The Portland string-band-turned-rock group's farewell tour, with Bay Area harmony trio Rainbow Girls opening. All ages; doors 8pm.

title: Fake TED Talks: Jonathan Coulton, Janeane Garofalo, Adam Savage & more (SF Sketchfest)
description: Comedians and guests including Jonathan Coulton, Janeane Garofalo, Laura Kightlinger, Adam Savage and Dulcé Sloan give rehearsed, fact-free parody TED talks. This is the late show; the 7pm show is already sold out.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Golden Gate Park, West End
venue: North (Dutch) Windmill, Queen Wilhelmina Garden (meeting point)
address: JFK Dr at Great Highway, San Francisco, CA 94121
description: A free volunteer-led walk at the ocean end of Golden Gate Park, from the Dutch Windmill past the Murphy Windmill to the Beach Chalet's 1930s murals. It covers how the sand dunes were turned into parkland and a dune village built from retired cable cars.

title: FOG Design+Art fair (Saturday, with FOG Talks)
venue: Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture (Festival + Gateway Pavilions)
description: SF Art Week's flagship fair of contemporary art and design galleries on the Fort Mason piers, benefiting SFMOMA. Saturday's ticket includes FOG Talks such as 'Only in San Francisco' with The Kitchen Sisters' Davia Nelson (1pm) and Marilyn Minter with SFMOMA's Janet Bishop (5pm).

title: Tea & Dandelion Chocolate pairing class (Tap Twice Tea)
description: A 90-minute tasting of five categories of tea, each paired with single-origin chocolate from Dandelion, led by a tea sourcer who has worked in the trade since 2009. It covers how tea is made and how to brew it well.

title: Tantra Speed Date: speed dating beyond small talk
description: A fully guided singles evening of playful, embodied connection exercises in place of the usual small-talk rounds, followed by matching. It's open to all adult ages (mostly 30s-50s per the FAQ), and most people come on their own.

title: The Brothers Comatose
description: SF's own rowdy five-piece string band plays bluegrass, country and rock 'n' roll at full volume, one of the most fun live nights in town. Night two of two (Fri Jan 22 too). All ages; doors 8:30pm.

title: SF City Guides free walking tour: Haight-Ashbury
description: A two-hour walk through the 1967 Summer of Love neighbourhood, past the Straight Theater and the Grateful Dead's old haunts, ending near Waller and Ashbury.

title: Irish trad seisiún at the Plough and Stars
description: The weekly Sunday-afternoon instrumental Irish session at SF's best-known trad pub. Come to listen, or bring an instrument and join in.

title: Angela Autumn (Throwin' Bo's live music at the 4 Star)
description: Appalachian-rooted country-folk singer Angela Autumn, 'The Rose of Appalachia', plays an intimate Sunday show inside the Outer Richmond's old cinema. Doors 7pm, music 8pm.

title: Gerald Henig: Little-Known (and Shocking) Revelations About America's Presidents
description: Cal State East Bay historian Gerald Henig shares funny, tragic and bizarre stories from his award-finalist book America's Presidents: What Your History Teacher Never Told You, on why so few presidents achieved greatness. In-person only.

title: SalsaCrazy Mondays: salsa lesson + salsa/bachata dancing
description: A beginner salsa lesson (no partner or experience required), then salsa and bachata social dancing at the Inner Richmond's long-running Monday dance night. 21+.

title: Bebel Gilberto: 25 Years of Tanto Tempo
description: The Brazilian singer marks 25 years of her electronic bossa-nova classic Tanto Tempo. Doors 7pm, 21+; on sale Fri 11/6.

title: Long Now Talk: Dakota Gruener on sunlight reflection research
address: Pier 2, Fort Mason Center, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: Dakota Gruener leads Reflective, a nonprofit speeding up rigorous, transparent research on sunlight reflection (solar geoengineering); she was previously founding director of ID2020. Tickets weren't on sale yet when checked.

title: Am I the A*Hole? Courtroom Comedy Show (SF Sketchfest)
description: Comedians argue petty real-life disputes in a mock courtroom and the audience delivers the verdict. You can submit your own case before the show.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: What Is Liberalism? with Prof. Brian Weiner (Manny's)
description: The first of USF professor Brian Weiner's four-part 'Political Ideologies 101' series at Manny's, on the history, meanings and tensions of liberalism. It's a short Wednesday-evening talk with discussion in a sociable Mission civic café.

title: Pollinated: Magic Theatre salon (cross-disciplinary conversation)
description: A new monthly salon for 75–100 guests with cocktails, a short live artistic piece and a conversation among four or five people from very different fields. It's built for mingling across disciplines. Venue is listed only as Magic Theatre, so check the ticket for the exact location.

title: The Bay Area Pun-Off (SF Sketchfest)
description: A pun tournament with elimination rounds, now in its eleventh year after starting in an Oakland living room, hosted by a former O. Henry Pun-Off champion. It bills itself as one of the warmest, nerdiest comedy rooms in the city, and last year's opening night sold out.

title: Jon Bryant
description: Canadian indie-folk singer-songwriter Jon Bryant previews his back-to-roots album Harbour in the 1907 basement speakeasy. Tickets are 'on sale soon' as of Oct 30; 21+, doors 7pm.

title: BD in the YUniverse: BD Wong performs Charles Yu stories
description: Tony winner and SF native BD Wong performs four funny, moving short stories by National Book Award winner Charles Yu. Four performances only, Jan 28-31, in A.C.T.'s experimental ACTivate series.

title: Milonga Malevaje (Thursday tango at the Verdi Club)
description: The weekly Argentine tango milonga on the Verdi Club's historic sprung dance floor. It's a social dance for those who already know some tango, and also a good place to watch and meet the local scene.

title: City of the Sun with Valley Wolf
description: NYC instrumental guitar band City of the Sun play cinematic, surf and desert-rock songs from their Phil Ek-produced album Under the Moon. Modesto Latin-psych band Valley Wolf open. The show was rescheduled from Oct 21.

title: The Improvised Shakespeare Company (SF Sketchfest)
description: The troupe improvises a full Shakespearean play in Elizabethan verse from a single audience-suggested title. A Sketchfest favourite.

title: Bachata Lab: Friday bachata classes (3 levels) + social
description: Beginner, intermediate and advanced bachata classes at 8pm with constant partner rotation, then a social until 1am. A very easy place to meet people.

title: Ty Segall
description: The prolific garage-rock hero, an SF scene alumnus, in a small room: the first of two nights at the Chapel (Sat Jan 30 too). All ages; doors 7:30pm.

title: Heart-Throb Slasher: an improvised 80s horror movie with Lane Moore (SF Sketchfest)
description: The Tinder Live creator runs a choose-your-own-adventure improvised 80s horror film, with the audience deciding who lives using 80s teen board games. Griffin Newman guests in this intimate North Beach listening room.

title: Stamptown at SF Sketchfest 2027, hosted by Zach Zucker
description: Zach Zucker's chaotic, character-heavy alt-comedy showcase, one of the first SF Sketchfest 2027 shows on sale. The festival runs Jan 14-31, and its initial lineup drops Nov 13. 18+; doors 6pm.

title: Sketch & Improv Showcase: emerging teams (SF Sketchfest)
description: Up-and-coming sketch and improv teams Ephemera (NY), Go Tech Yourself (SF), Hot Dog Tony (Greensboro) and Worlds Most Best (LA) share a small Mission stage. It's a cheap way into the festival and the work of new performers.

title: The Arcadian Wild: Make It Out Alive Tour
description: Nashville indie-folk trio with close harmonies and acoustic strings, in the wood-panelled upstairs hall. Doors 8pm, show 9pm, 21+.

title: Vietnamese New Year (Tết) Street Festival in Little Saigon
description: The Southeast Asian Community Center's free Lunar New Year street festival, with lion dances, traditional music, an Áo Dài pageant and Vietnamese food stalls. It runs a week before Lunar New Year (6 Feb).

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with a free beginner lesson from Hep Jen at noon. Partners rotate, so you don't need to bring one. Weather permitting.

title: Porchlight storytelling: Sketchfest edition
description: SF's 23-year-old storytelling series, where six people tell ten-minute true stories without notes and Marc Capelle plays music. This edition features Joel Kim Booster, Guy Branum, River Butcher, Larry Mullins and Amy Schneider.

title: Contact Improvisation class + jam at The Castro Room
description: The 1st-Monday SF contact improv night: a class from 7:45 to 8:45pm, then an open jam with live music until 10:15. Beginners are welcome.

title: Vansire with Eliza McLamb
description: The Minnesota dream-pop duo Vansire, with indie songwriter Eliza McLamb, at Bimbo's. Doors 7pm, all ages; price per The List.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance on the Verdi Club's 2,500 sq ft floor. The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: Figure drawing at Monument SF (Sketchboard Co.)
description: A two-hour drop-in life drawing session with a model, run by Sketchboard Co. in SoMa. All levels are welcome; bring your own materials and book ahead on Square.

title: BFF.fm Karaoke at the Make-Out Room
description: Free karaoke night hosted by the DJs of community radio station BFF.fm in the Mission's favourite small room. Doors at 6pm, singing from 8pm.

title: Cécile McLorin Salvant
description: The Grammy-winning jazz vocalist opens a four-night SFJAZZ run (Feb 4-7). The cheapest seats ($50) fit the budget.

title: AJJ at Great American Music Hall
description: Phoenix folk-punk band AJJ (formerly Andrew Jackson Jihad) bring their wry, literate songs to SF's ornate 1907 music hall. Doors 7pm, show 8pm, all ages.

title: Bachata Lab: Friday bachata classes (3 levels) + social
description: The weekly Friday bachata night: concurrent beginner, intermediate and advanced classes from 8pm with partner rotation, then social dancing until 1am.

title: About Last Night: one-night-stand storytelling show
description: Real people tell true stories about horrifying one-night stands, awkward hookups and regrettable romps at this monthly Mission storytelling night. Doors 7pm, show 8pm.

title: The Commons monthly picnic in Alamo Square (February)
address: Alamo Square Park, San Francisco, CA
description: The SF Commons' February picnic: blankets, shared snacks, lawn games and live music in Alamo Square. It's a relaxed drop-in way to meet people, and you're asked to bring a game, book or snack to share.

title: The Sways (Arizona folk-rock trio) at Cafe du Nord
description: A rising indie folk-rock trio from the mountains of Northern Arizona, playing songs about friendship, fatherhood and everyday life in the basement room. Doors 7pm, show 8pm, 21+.

title: RENT at San Francisco Playhouse (closing night)
description: The final performance of Bill English's production of Jonathan Larson's rock musical about young artists in New York's East Village. The theatre calendar lists two performances on Feb 6, and Saturday evenings start at 8pm.

title: SF Salsa Social: beginner class + salsa & mambo dancing
description: The first-Sunday salsa night at the Verdi Club: a beginner class at 7pm, then salsa and mambo social dancing. Easy to come solo.

title: Wolf Parade with Prairie Princess
description: The Montreal indie-rock band behind Apologies to the Queen Mary play the restored Castro Theatre. Doors 6pm, show 7pm, all ages. General sale opens Fri 13 Nov at 10am.

title: SalsaCrazy Mondays: salsa lesson + salsa/bachata dancing
description: A weekly Monday salsa night on Clement St: a beginner lesson with no partner needed, then social salsa and bachata dancing.

title: National Theatre Live: Hay Fever (Christine Baranski, Richard E. Grant)
description: A screening of the West End production of Noël Coward's comedy, filmed live, with Christine Baranski and Richard E. Grant. It plays in a 1910 neighbourhood cinema.

title: Andrea Gibson's Love Letter From The Afterlife (film + live orchestra)
description: A screening of the late poet Andrea Gibson's final live performance, with the Goosebump Orchestra playing Blake Neely's score live, plus poet Megan Falley and guests. It comes from the team behind Come See Me in the Good Light. General sale opens Fri 13 Nov.

title: Fat Tuesday Celebration with Rebirth Brass Band
description: New Orleans' Rebirth Brass Band plays Mardi Gras night, with NOLA food and drink specials and the East Bay Brass Band in the Curio bar. Doors 7pm.

title: Trivia Night at Manny's
description: Monthly team trivia night with prizes at the Mission's civic-minded café and event space. Solo arrivals can easily join a team and meet people.

title: Open Jazz Jam at The Lucky Horseshoe
description: A free open jazz jam in a Bernal Heights neighbourhood bar. Musicians sit in and everyone else listens over a drink.

title: The Milk Carton Kids at The Chapel
description: The Milk Carton Kids are a Grammy-nominated folk duo known for close two-part harmonies and intricate acoustic guitar. (((folkYEAH!))) presents them in the Chapel's converted mortuary hall, with doors at 7pm. All ages.

title: 16th Annual Salsa Rueda Festival
description: A four-day Cuban salsa and rueda festival (Thu-Sun) with 60+ workshops, a beginner bootcamp and nightly parties with bands and DJs. Buy a party pass to keep within budget.

title: Grace Hwang Lynch: How to Cook Rice (Omnivore Books author talk)
address: 3885A Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
description: Bay Area food writer Grace Hwang Lynch talks about her book on Asian American food and the care and feeding of an immigrant family, joined by Taiwanese American physician-chef Linda Shiue. It's a free talk in Noe Valley's food bookshop.

title: Milonga Malevaje (Thursday tango at the Verdi Club)
description: The weekly Argentine tango milonga on the Verdi Club's historic floor, a good night to watch and meet the local tango scene.

title: Bachata Lab: Friday bachata classes (3 levels) + social (pre-Valentine's)
description: Friday-night bachata on Valentine's weekend: classes at three levels, including a true beginner class, then a social dance until 1am. Partners rotate, so you can come solo.

title: Lael Neale with Spacemoth (solo)
description: Sub Pop's Lael Neale plays her hypnotic, omnichord-driven indie folk (folkYEAH! presents). Doors 7:30pm.

title: Richard Thompson & Band with Clayton Linthicum and Quinn Bachand
description: The Fairport Convention co-founder and British folk-rock guitar legend plays a seated show with his band. Doors 7pm; price per The List.

title: Michael Shannon & Jason Narducy and Friends play R.E.M.'s Document
description: Actor Michael Shannon and musician Jason Narducy (longtime Bob Mould bassist) front a band playing R.E.M.'s 1987 album Document, at the historic Fillmore. This is the second of two nights.

title: Jonathan Richman featuring Tommy Larkins
description: The Modern Lovers founder plays a warm, funny, mostly acoustic set with longtime drummer Tommy Larkins. The first of two nights at GAMH; doors 7pm.

title: Lindy in the Park: free swing dancing + beginner lesson (Valentine's Day)
venue: Golden Gate Park, JFK Drive (8th-10th Ave)
address: JFK Dr between 8th & 10th Ave (behind the de Young), San Francisco, CA
description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday since 1996 on car-free JFK Drive, with a free beginner lesson at noon. No partner needed; weather permitting.

title: Hello! Bachata & Kizomba Sunday (Valentine's Day)
description: A daytime bachata social (and kizomba upstairs) on the Verdi Club's two floors on Valentine's Day. Social, easy to join solo, and over by evening.

title: Valentine's Day 1940s Swing Dance aboard the USS Hornet (Death and Taxes Swing Band)
venue: USS Hornet Sea, Air & Space Museum
description: A 1940s Valentine's swing dance on a WWII aircraft carrier, with a short ship history talk, a 7pm beginner lesson and a big band until about 9pm, and the organisers say 'come as a couple or come to meet someone' (18+). It's in Alameda (East Bay), not reachable by BART: about 25 min by car or rideshare from SoMa through the Posey Tube, with free parking.

title: SalsaCrazy Mondays on Presidents' Day: salsa lesson + salsa/bachata dancing
description: The Monday salsa night on the Presidents' Day holiday: beginner and intermediate lessons early, then salsa and bachata social dancing until late. Many people come solo.

title: Free bluegrass jam & concert at Blondie's (Presidents' Day)
description: Blondie's weekly Monday night of local bluegrass, a concert plus open jam on Valencia St. Free with an Eventbrite RSVP.

title: Jazz at the Make-Out Room
description: A free Tuesday jazz night in the Mission bar (doors 6pm, music 7pm). An easy weeknight drop-in.

title: Asian Singles & Those Who Love Them: singles mixer at ERIA Marina
description: A post-Valentine's singles mixer with an icebreaker mixer game. 'Singles of all ethnicities are warmly welcome' and 'adults of all ages', and proceeds benefit the Seva Foundation.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The weekly Tuesday live-band swing dance at the historic Verdi Club, with a different band each week (not yet announced). The drop-in beginner lesson at 9pm is included and no partner is needed.

title: Figure drawing at Monument SF (Sketchboard Co.)
description: Sketchboard Co.'s Wednesday drop-in life drawing session with a live model at Monument in SoMa, running two hours with short and long poses. All levels are welcome.

title: City Arts & Lectures: Dr. Orna Guralnik
description: The psychoanalyst from the docuseries 'Couples Therapy' talks about her work and her new book 'Couples'. Tickets aren't on sale yet ('coming soon').

title: Jess Williamson with Andrew Sa (Noise Pop 2027)
description: The Texan singer-songwriter's country-tinged indie folk, on the opening night of Noise Pop 2027 (Feb 18-28). Doors 7pm.

title: Lizard Boy at SF Playhouse (first performance)
description: First performance of SF Playhouse's run of the indie-rock musical about a reclusive young man who risks everything on a first date, a story about identity, love and being seen. The run continues until 3 April.

title: Fink with Maggie Koerner
description: Fin Greenall's Fink plays his 1974-style folk album The City Is Coming to Erase It All, with New Orleans singer Maggie Koerner. Doors 8:30pm; price per The List.

title: San Francisco Chinese New Year Parade (Year of the Ram)
address: Second St & Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105
description: The big Lunar New Year night parade of dragons, lion dancers, floats and drummers, stepping off at 2nd & Market a few minutes from home. Chinatown's Community Street Fair runs the same weekend (Sat-Sun Feb 20-21) on Grant Ave.

title: Mucha Salsa+ social (free beginner class)
description: A not-for-profit Sunday salsa social at the Verdi Club. Beginner and intermediate classes run 7-8pm and are included, then DJ social dancing until 11:30pm.

title: Into It. Over It. with From Indian Lakes and Tenebre (Noise Pop)
description: Evan Weiss's indie/emo project headlines a Noise Pop 2027 show in the ornate Tenderloin hall. Doors at 7pm, show at 8pm.

title: Roar Shack Live!: Timo Andres
description: The acclaimed composer-pianist gives an intimate new-music recital in a small SoMa space off Market. Free with an RSVP.

title: Cut Worms (solo) (Noise Pop 2027)
description: Max Clarke's Cut Worms plays a solo set of Everly Brothers-flavoured indie folk-pop in the Swedish American Hall, as part of Noise Pop 2027.

title: Amory Lovins on Disruptive Energy Futures
description: Physicist Amory Lovins revisits his famous 1976 Foreign Affairs essay on America's energy paths and where the energy transition could go next. Doors and check-in at 6pm.

title: Drop-In Circling Workshop (Berkeley)
description: The Circling Institute's in-person drop-in evening of the Original Circling approach and authentic relating, a guided practice in presence and connection with strangers. Advance registration is required and the last one sold out a week ahead; doors close at 7:10pm. East Bay: BART to Downtown Berkeley (~25 min), then bus or bike to West Berkeley.

title: Sylvie
description: LA band Sylvie's warm, '70s-style Laurel Canyon soft rock and folk (folkYEAH! presents). Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: Radio Free Alice (Noise Pop 2027)
description: Melbourne guitar band touring its Atlantic Records debut, What's In Between, at the small Hayes Valley room as part of Noise Pop 2027. All ages; doors 7pm, show 7:45pm.

title: Deerhoof with Earthball and Gumby's Junk
description: SF-born art-rock band Deerhoof plays a hometown show at the Great American Music Hall. Doors 7pm.

title: Timnit Gebru: The Rise of AI and the Radicalization of a Tech Idealist
description: The AI-ethics researcher, who left Google's Ethical AI team after warning about large language models, talks about her career and the AI industry. Doors 6:30pm.

title: Asaf Avidan: Into the Great Abyss solo tour
description: The gravel-voiced Israeli singer-songwriter plays a solo show of folk, blues and jazz-tinged songs. Doors 7:30pm, all ages.

title: Tommy and Saundra O'Sullivan in concert (UICC)
description: An evening concert of Irish music with Tommy and Saundra O'Sullivan at the United Irish Cultural Center, billed as a warm-up for the St Patrick's season. It's a good way into SF's Irish community.

title: Here We Go Magic: 15th Anniversary of A Different Ship (Noise Pop 2027)
description: Luke Temple's Brooklyn indie band revisits its Nigel Godrich-produced album A Different Ship, as part of Noise Pop. Doors 7pm.

title: Cloud Nothings
description: Cleveland indie-rock band Cloud Nothings bring their fast, noisy guitar songs to the small Rickshaw Stop. Doors 8pm, all ages.

title: San Francisco Slavic Festival 2027: food, music & dance
description: A weekend culture festival (27-28 Feb) with nonstop live folk dancing, folk music and traditional Slavic food. The page is still a 'save the date', so ticket details aren't out yet.

title: Upswing Series: Tyreek McDole / Isaiah Collier
description: A double bill in Terence Blanchard's rising-stars series: vocalist Tyreek McDole and spiritual-jazz saxophonist Isaiah Collier.

title: Caroline Rose: Uncle Carol's World of Fun Tour (Noise Pop 2027)
description: The genre-hopping indie songwriter plays the Castro Theatre for Noise Pop 2027. Doors 7pm, all ages; price per The List.

title: An Evening with Lambchop accompanied by Free Key Choir (Noise Pop 2027)
description: Kurt Wagner's Nashville band Lambchop plays its gospel-tinged new album with Oakland's experimental Free Key Choir, inside Grace Cathedral. It's a one-off Noise Pop festival highlight; the ride up Nob Hill is steep.

title: Contact Improvisation class with Dai & Wei at ODC
description: A weekly Sunday-afternoon contact improvisation class at ODC in the Mission, taught by Daiane Lopes da Silva and Weidong Yang. Beginners are welcome.

title: Onóir in Concert: 2027 West Coast premiere (matinee)
description: Irish group Onóir plays the second of two '2027 West Coast Premiere' concerts at the United Irish Cultural Center near Ocean Beach. An early start to the St Patrick's season.

title: Gibby Haynes: Butthole Surfers Mania (Noise Pop 2027)
description: Butthole Surfers frontman Gibby Haynes leads a night of the band's chaotic psych-punk songs at the ornate Great American Music Hall, closing out Noise Pop. Doors 7pm.

title: Contact Improvisation class + jam at The Castro Room
description: The 1st-Monday SF contact improv night: a class from 7:45 to 8:45pm, then an open jam with live music until 10:15. Beginners are welcome.

title: Valley: DYNTBE? The Tour, with Moody Joody
description: The Toronto indie-pop band plays the NoPa club, with Moody Joody opening. Doors at 7:30pm, all ages.

title: Wasia Project: Nocturne Live 2027
description: London sibling duo Wasia Project (Olivia Hardy and Will Gao) play their debut album Nocturne, which mixes classical piano, cinematic pop and electronica. Doors 7pm, all ages.

title: The Bad News Bears: A Musical (A.C.T. world premiere, preview)
description: World-premiere musical of the 1976 film about a washed-up ballplayer coaching a team of Little League misfits. This is a preview-week performance; the run lasts until 4 April.

title: Chip Bergh: The Levi's Story
description: Former Levi Strauss & Co. CEO Chip Bergh talks about rebuilding one of San Francisco's most iconic companies. Doors and check-in at 5:30pm.

title: Bonny Doon at Kilowatt
description: Detroit band Bonny Doon play hazy, laid-back indie folk-rock. The gig is in the stage room at Kilowatt, the 16th St bar that was the original home of Noise Pop. 21+.

title: Fog City Improv
description: A free Friday improv comedy show in the North Beach club that hosts Cat's Corner swing on Wednesdays.

title: Required Taste & Friends (improv)
description: A Saturday evening of improv from the long-running SF troupe Required Taste and guest teams at Endgames' Mission theatre.

title: Crooked Fingers and Jim Ward at Kilowatt
description: Eric Bachmann's Crooked Fingers (indie folk-rock, ex-Archers of Loaf) share a bill with Jim Ward of At the Drive-In and Sparta. It's a small-room show at the Mission's Kilowatt. 21+.

title: SF Salsa Social: beginner class + salsa & mambo dancing
description: The first-Sunday salsa and mambo social at the Verdi Club: a beginner class at 7pm, then social dancing from 8 to 11:30pm.

title: SalsaCrazy Mondays: salsa lesson + salsa/bachata dancing
description: Monday salsa classes for all levels, then salsa and bachata social dancing in the club afterwards. One of the easiest ways to start dancing in SF and meet people.

title: National Theatre Live: The Motive and the Cue (Vogue Theatre)
description: A screening of Sam Mendes's Olivier-winning London production, with Mark Gatiss as John Gielgud directing Johnny Flynn's Richard Burton in a 1964 Broadway Hamlet. Jack Thorne wrote it, and CinemaSF passes are accepted.

title: Happy Endings: writers' showdown at the Make-Out Room
description: Five writers perform new work on a shared theme, competing for the approval of an appointed committee. A literary night with a comedy edge in a Mission bar.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: San Francisco's weekly Tuesday swing dance with a live band and a 9pm beginner lesson. Easy to show up alone and dance with strangers.

title: Christian Kuria: EAST TOUR
description: Soulful singer-songwriter Christian Kuria brings his East Tour to the classic North Beach supper-club room. Doors 7pm, show 8pm, all ages.

title: Katherine Li: I love you, or whatever Tour (Cafe du Nord)
description: Toronto singer-songwriter Katherine Li plays heartfelt, rom-com-flavoured pop songs in the basement room on Market St. All ages; doors 7pm.

title: Lindsey Caplan & Anthony Veneziale: The Art and Science of What Moves Us
description: The screenwriter turned organizational psychologist talks about her book Moved (why information alone rarely changes people) with Freestyle Love Supreme co-creator Anthony Veneziale. Doors 5:30pm, then a book signing at 7pm.

title: Moontricks with Will Evans
description: Moontricks headline Great American Music Hall, the ornate Tenderloin room, with Will Evans supporting. Doors 7pm, show 8pm.

title: Troilus and Cressida (A.C.T. OUT Tour preview)
description: A fast, in-the-round, 90-minute modern-verse staging (Play On Shakespeare translation) of Shakespeare's cynical war tragicomedy, in the Strand's intimate Rueff space. This is the first public preview.

title: Pi Day at the Exploratorium (its birthplace)
address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero at Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: Pi Day was invented at the Exploratorium in 1988, and the museum still celebrates it with a procession around the Pi Shrine, slices of pie and maths exhibits. It's a quirky slice of SF science culture on the morning the clocks go forward.

title: Hello! Bachata Sunday at the Verdi Club
description: A daytime bachata social on two floors of the Verdi Club, over by evening. Social and easy to join solo.

title: Contact Improvisation class + jam at The Castro Room
description: SF's 1st and 3rd Monday contact improv night: an hour's beginner-friendly class from 7:45pm flows into a jam with live music until 10:15pm. Teachers rotate, and the SF CI WhatsApp group posts who's on.

title: Free bluegrass jam & concert at Blondie's
description: Blondie's free Monday bluegrass night on Valencia St: some of the Bay Area's best local pickers play a set and jam. Easy, friendly, no cover.

title: Long Now Talk: Silvana Konermann on CRISPR and Alzheimer's
address: Pier 2, Fort Mason Center, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: Long Now's monthly talk: Arc Institute scientist Silvana Konermann on gene-editing approaches to Alzheimer's disease. Tickets 'on sale soon' when checked.

title: Bess Atwell
description: English indie-folk singer-songwriter Bess Atwell plays the small Hayes Valley room.

title: St Patrick's Day: The Rockers (Thin Lizzy tribute) at The Chapel
description: On St Patrick's night, a Bay Area band plays the songs of Ireland's great rock band, from the classics to the deep cuts, with Coffin Hunters supporting. Doors at 7pm, all ages.

title: Jake Lambert: The Sunshine Kid (A.C.T. Strand)
description: British comic Jake Lambert, called 'a joke machine' by The Telegraph and seen on Live at the Apollo, brings his rapid-fire storytelling show to A.C.T.'s Strand for one night only.

title: Helena Deland at The Chapel
description: Montreal singer-songwriter Helena Deland plays an intimate indie-folk set at The Chapel, presented by (((folkYEAH!))). Doors 7pm, show 8pm, all ages.

title: Bachata Lab: Friday bachata classes (3 levels) + social
description: Weekly Friday bachata classes in three concurrent levels, followed by a social dance. A beginner-friendly way to fill an empty Friday.

title: Teenage Fanclub
description: The Glasgow guitar-pop band led by Norman Blake and Raymond McGinley, still writing jangly, harmony-rich songs nearly four decades on. Doors 7pm.

title: The Music of Tom Verlaine (Jimmy Rip, Jay Dee Daugherty, Jackson Smith, Chris Lightcap)
description: Longtime collaborators from Television, the Tom Verlaine Band and the Patti Smith Group play songs from across Verlaine's career. It's a tribute from people who played them with him. Doors at 8pm.

title: Troilus and Cressida: opening night (A.C.T. OUT Tour)
description: Opening night of A.C.T. and Play On Shakespeare's fast, in-the-round modern-verse staging of Shakespeare's cynical war tragicomedy, in the Strand's intimate Rueff space.

title: Mucha Salsa+ at the Verdi Club (free beginner class + social)
description: iHeartMambo's not-for-profit salsa social: beginner and intermediate salsa classes at 7pm, included in entry, then DJ social dancing. Friendly, community-run crowd.

title: SalsaCrazy Mondays: salsa lesson + salsa/bachata dancing
description: Monday salsa night on Clement St: a beginner salsa lesson (no partner needed), then salsa and bachata social dancing until late. 21+.

title: City Arts & Lectures: Alison Roman
description: Cook and writer Alison Roman talks about turning internet food culture into a career and real-world places, the line between recipe and narrative writing, and keeping a creative life going offline. It's an onstage conversation at City Arts & Lectures.

title: Zephyr Teachout: Anti-Monopoly, a Citizen's Guide (Commonwealth Club)
venue: Commonwealth Club World Affairs (Toni Rembe Rock Auditorium)
description: Fordham law professor Zephyr Teachout explains how ordinary people can push back against corporate monopoly power. Doors 5:30pm, talk 6-7pm, then a book signing.

title: Drop-In Circling Workshop (Berkeley, March)
description: The Circling Institute's monthly in-person evening of authentic relating and the Original Circling approach. Register in advance, since the last one sold out a week ahead; doors close at 7:10pm. East Bay: take BART to Downtown Berkeley (~25 min), then bus or bike to West Berkeley.

title: Woodchopper's Ball: live-band swing night
description: The Verdi Club's weekly Tuesday swing dance with a different live band each week. A drop-in beginner lesson from 9:00 to 9:15pm is included, and no partner is needed.

title: Pollinated: interdisciplinary salon at Magic Theatre
description: Magic Theatre's salon series brings 75-100 guests together for cocktails, a short live artistic piece and a conversation among four or five unlikely voices, such as an AI researcher and a filmmaker. It's built for mixing with people outside your usual circle. The listing doesn't name the room, so check your ticket.

title: Charlotte Adigéry & Bolis Pupul at Great American Music Hall
description: The Belgian duo play witty, danceable electro-pop on their Mainland Madinina tour, in GAMH's ornate old ballroom. Doors at 7pm, all ages.

title: Darra Goldstein: Cultured (Omnivore Books author talk)
address: 3885A Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94131
description: Gastronomica founding editor Darra Goldstein presents Cultured, a global guide to fermenting, pickling and preserving, from quick pickles to kimchi and preserved lemons. Free at Noe Valley's food bookshop.

title: Fenne Lily at Rickshaw Stop
description: English singer-songwriter Fenne Lily plays hushed, wry indie folk. This is a headline show in the Rickshaw Stop's small room. Doors at 7pm, all ages.

title: Wild Pink with Truth Club at Cafe du Nord
description: (((folkYEAH!))) presents NYC band Wild Pink, whose expansive, novelistic indie rock sits between Americana and heartland rock. They play the basement supper-club room at Cafe du Nord. Doors at 8pm, 21+.

title: Thomas Dollbaum live at the 4 Star Theater
description: New Orleans-based alt-country and indie-rock storyteller Thomas Dollbaum plays songs from Birds of Paradise, cut in four days in Mississippi with a band that included Jake (MJ) Lenderman. It's an intimate Throwin' Bo's show in a neighbourhood cinema. Doors at 7pm.

title: Contact Improvisation class with Dai & Wei at ODC
description: A Sunday-afternoon contact improvisation class at ODC in the Mission, taught by Daiane Lopes da Silva and Weidong Yang. It's a relaxed, beginner-friendly way into SF's CI scene.

title: Dogpark with The Rose Hips
description: A New York band that started at the University of Richmond and plays riff-driven melodic rock with satirical lyrics about money, fame and corporate life. All ages; doors 7:30pm.

title: Camel Power Club
description: A French duo playing sunny, cinematic indie and dream pop that mixes folk, 60s British rock and surf. 18+; doors 7:30pm.

title: Perfect Daughter at San Francisco Playhouse (world premiere)
description: Chloé Hung's new play about a father who works with a scientist to build an AI version of his daughter, then keeps adjusting her life to get it 'just right'. This is a Thursday evening show in the run's final week, at the Creativity Theater in Yerba Buena Gardens.

title: Delta Sleep with Pure Hex
description: The UK math-rock band Delta Sleep, with Bay Area shoegaze band Pure Hex opening. All ages, standing; doors 7:30pm.

title: Butcher Brown
description: Richmond, Virginia's Butcher Brown, a band that blends jazz, funk and hip-hop and is known for loose, energetic live shows. 21+; doors 8:30pm.

title: Purpose Alignment Circle at The Commons (April)
description: A facilitated small-group circle for candid conversation about work, purpose and what you actually want, aimed at people questioning their path or weighing a change. The host says it isn't a networking event.

title: Long Now Talk: Meenakshi Wadhwa on meteorites, Moon rocks and the early Solar System
address: Pier 2, Fort Mason Center, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: Planetary scientist Meenakshi Wadhwa, director of Scripps Institution of Oceanography and former head of ASU's School of Earth and Space Exploration, studies how the Solar System formed using meteorites and samples returned by spacecraft. Tickets aren't on sale yet.
